name: number-ticker

frames.best_why: The numbers have nearly reached their targets, showing the finished values clearly.

tagline: Numbers spring upward from zero to their target values.
summary: An animated figure that counts up or down to a target with a spring easing the first time it scrolls into view, formatted with commas and optional decimals.
appearance: Three large white numbers stacked on black, each above a small grey label: a user count, a percentage and a dollar figure. The digits are tight, bold and tabular.
behaviour: Each number rises from zero toward its target once it enters the viewport, decelerating into place and then staying fixed.
demo_content: Three stats labelled Active Users, Uptime and Revenue with values like 12,500, 99.0% and $4,820,000.
use_when: A stats section should make its numbers feel alive when it comes into view.
avoid_when: The value changes live: it animates only once on first view and ignores later updates.
customise: The target value, start value, direction, delay and decimal places are props; formatting is fixed to en-US with commas.
weight_why: One span whose text is updated by a single spring value.

a11y.note: Plain text that rewrites many times a second can make screen readers repeat values; no reduced-motion guard.

polish_why: Clean, readable numbers with a smooth spring; the three-stat demo is plain but effective.
